mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP above its 6-month moving average indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of GDP growth above its 6-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives down S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 6% indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and lower S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of high unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth exceeds 5% over a 6-month period, it indicates increased supply chain activity, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising housing starts and increasing retail sales indicates a strong demand for goods and services, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high housing starts and retail sales (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate below 2% indicates an easing monetary cycle, leading to increased borrowing and spending, which in turn drives up S&P 500 prices over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low federal funds rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between low unemployment rates and high payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and higher S&P 500 prices over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of low unemployment and high payroll employment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in consumer price index above its 6-month moving average indicates increased demand for goods and services, leading to higher S&P 500 prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of high consumer price index growth (t-test p > 0.05).
